newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends weaker at 493.75/494.75/dlr.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends weaker at 493.75/494.75/dlr.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed marginally weaker at 493.75/494.75 per dollar Friday as the Central Bank met heavy corporate demand to prevent a steeper slide of the local currency, traders said.
The bolivar closed at 493.25/494.25 Wednesday. Markets were closed Thursday for a national holiday.
"The Central Bank came in during the afternoon with enough strength to calm the market and bring the exchange rate down," one trader said.
Heavy dollar demand and scarce offer from banks had seen the exchange rate creep above 495 bolivars per dollar in the morning, traders added.
Traders said the Central Bank was struggling to soak up excess levels of liquidity which had placed additional pressure on the local currency.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
